concerns.text: The plan relies on synthetic fMRI data generated from noise estimates of real datasets. While this enables controlled effect sizes, it may not capture the full spatial, temporal, and physiological complexity of authentic BOLD signals, limiting the external validity of the resulting power curves for real‑world studies.

Replication success is defined with an arbitrary ±20 % magnitude tolerance relative to the known ground‑truth effect size. No justification or sensitivity analysis for this threshold is provided, and the choice could substantially bias estimated power.

Only 50 bootstrap iterations per configuration are planned. For low effect sizes this may yield unstable empirical replication probabilities and wide confidence intervals; a larger number of iterations (e.g., ≥ 200) is typically recommended for reliable power estimation.

The design assumes orthogonal predictors (sample size, smoothing kernel, SNR), yet SNR levels are derived from the same datasets used to simulate effect sizes, potentially inducing collinearity. VIF monitoring is mentioned but no explicit strategy to decorrelate these variables is described.
